messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] formatting issue in csv part5 Person/day summary - some cells formatted as numbers others as general
parts:
Dear Tin,

The file you shared is not a file generated by GGIR. GGIR does not generate xlsx files.
Probably you converted the file tot xlsx and that is where the formatting got messed up.
When you load GGIR generated csv files always make sure that the column and decimal separators are correctly recognised before you export it to other file formats.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

Hi All,

I have an issue in part5 with day and personsummary of PA data analysis with actigraph and would appreciate your help. In the csv out file with results "part5Daysummary" some cells are formatted as general and some as numbers. It then happens that for one patient there are e.g. 54min in moderate PA, but 115000min of light PA (instead of 115min). Cels seem to be differently formatted at random (for patient X, 3 cells are well formated as number, but then one is as general). Is there a way to correct for that?

Thank you for help! :)

I am attaching an example from my excel part5_personsummary and my R code.

Dear Tin,

NEVER delete posts from the google group. The reason we have this google group in public is to allow others to learn from questions and answers asked. I do not respond to your questions to only help you but to help everyone with the same question in the future. Also keep in mind that this is an email list as well, so all messages end up in peoples inbox which you cannot delete.

If a problem is solved report this back to the google group such that everyone knows that the problem was solved. This is how Open source software communities work. Community effort to report and help solve problems is crucial.

Please do not send me a personal message with additional questions, unless you are interested in hiring me to work on them. Just start a new thread in the google group and wait for someone to reply.

Thanks,

Vincent

On Wednesday, 24 January 2024 at 9:50 AM, Tin GOJEVIC <tin.g...@uhasselt.be> wrote:
Thank you Vincent, I resolved this yesterday and it worked fine so deleted the post from the group. There is another dilemma that I have in terms of wear time analysis. I wonder if the variable Dur_day_min reports valid wear time or stg else (i.e. what is awake time)?
My patients carry gt3x 10h/day, but I get Dur_day_min of 16-19hours in average (i.e. over 1000 minutes in all subjects for all days) and I do not understand how can this be as the visual inspection of patient files shows a few hours less of wear time per day? Shouldn't the variable Dur_day_spt_min for my patients amount to the total hours they wore the monitor(i.e. 10-19h/day), and then be divided into active time and sleep? At the moment Dur_day_min + Dur_spt_min equals 24h, but my patients only wear monitor 10 to cca 19h/d.

I wish to report in my study the average wear time expressed in minutes/day.

Thank you,
Tin
